sentences.text: 2. Adrian is interviewing Jessica Becker.
Jessica has written a book about culture and fitness in Asia.
Listen to the interview and complete the information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Can Jessica, and thanks for joining us.
Hi Adrian. Thank you for inviting me.
Your new book, Exercise in Asia is out now.
Can you tell our audience something about it?
and taiko festivals are very popular all over Japan.
What makes these festivals so popular?
Taiko drumming has a long tradition.
In the past people believed that drumming was a way to communicate with the gods.
Communicate with the gods?
Yes, taiko drums are really loud.
That’s why they are so loud, so that the gods can hear, What happens at a Taeko festival?
I'm imagining the band marching and carrying their drums through the streets.
Oh no, they’re too large to carry.
Some of the drums can weigh up to 400 kilograms.
Imagine lifting that.
that! So, for the festival, they place the drums on the moving platform.
That way, everyone can see.
Jessica, I’m interested in the really big drums.
Let’s talk about them.
Those big drums are called o-daiko, and, as I mentioned, they’re really heavy.
What else is special about them?
them? Well, interestingly, in the past they were made from a single piece of wood.
That's amazing, given how big they are.
Are they still made from a single piece of wood?
Oh no. It’s difficult to find the right kind of trees now.
Jessica, your book and our podcast is about fitness, so I’m very interested to know, is it a good workout to play the drums?
For sure. If you want to be good, you have to use your whole body.
Not just your arms?
No, your whole body.
So it’s a great workout, actually.
Another chapter in your book was about k -pop dancing.
Everybody knows k -pop, but you're saying it’s also good exercise?
Yes, k -pop has become a popular fitness activity ever since Korean boy bands added street dance to their performances.
I love street dance.
So, if I’m in Korea, I can just join in with some K -pop dancing on the street, can I?
Yes, you can, but you should absolutely take some classes first.
That sounds useful, but I've never joined a dance class before.
Any tips? My first suggestion is to warm up before you get to class.
class, The dance routines can be pretty energetic and there may not be enough time to warm up when the class starts.
What about clothing?
Do I need to dress like a pop star?
You don’t need trendy clothes, they just need to be comfortable.
Wear clothes that let you move freely.
And what about footwear?
I usually dance at home and my slippers.
Can I wear those?
Er. no, not slippers.
You can wear any kind of sport shoes.
Right, any kind of sport shoes.
I’ll remember, But what will I actually learn in class?
us. You'll learn some basic moves and some dance routines.
But changing from one move to another can be tricky, so what you really have to learn is quick thinking.
Why’s that? Well, to correct any problems in your moves and routines, you'll have to make some quick decisions, The music won't stop for you.
That sounds like a useful life skill, Jessica, not just for K -pop dancing.
Indeed. I was surprised to read that another activity you participated in was running a marathon in Thailand.
Thailand is such a hot country.
How do you cope with running in that heat?
heat. Thailand is hot, so marathons usually start while it’s still dark, before sunrise.
That’s so early.
But it must still be hot.
How do you keep cool?
Well, usually the organizers give you wet towels if you want them.
That are so beautiful.
The scenery is gorgeous.
Sounds great. Do you have any tips for running a marathon there?
Yes. as you say, the marathons are very popular.
So, make sure you sign up early.
OK, that makes sense.
Anything else? Well, the courses can be beautiful, but they also be quite demanding.
Check the difficulty of the course before signing up.
Well, that’s some good advice for our listeners to think about, Jessica.
A big thank you for coming on the podcast today and good luck with the book.
Any time. It’s been a pleasure.
